anomalies.observed: U2 (MAX3485) is assigned footprint Package_SO:SO-8_5.3x6.2mm_P1.27mm, a wide-body 5.3 mm SO-8. The library part's footprint filter is SOIC*3.9x4.9mm*P1.27mm*, which is the narrow 3.9 mm SOIC-8 body.
anomalies.expected: The MAX3485 in its SOIC-8 package should use the 3.9 mm narrow-body SOIC-8 footprint that matches the library filter, so the pad row spacing and body match the part.
anomalies.impact: If the part is the narrow SOIC-8 package, the pads will not match its leads, so the transceiver may not solder reliably or may not make contact, leaving the serial bus driver non-functional.

anomalies.observed: R15 (0 Ω) shorts the two servo signal pins Net-(J9-Pin_3) and Net-(J1-Pin_3). R22 (0 Ω) also ties Net-(J9-Pin_3) to the RS-485 A line /NET0040. At the same time, the PWM series resistors R9 (1k) and R3 (1k) and the GPIO select jumpers R11, R24, R18 and R19 are all populated, so both PWM GPIO nets are still wired to the servo pins.
anomalies.expected: The specification says the two servo interface modes are mutually exclusive. In PWM mode the bridge and bus jumpers must be open so the two channels stay independent. In serial mode the bridge and bus jumpers are closed and the PWM path is disconnected.

evidence.quote: PWM mode (populate R3/R4, and the appropriate R9–R12 pair for the Core variant; leave R13/R14 open)
two mutually-exclusive servo interface modes, selected at assembly time by populating different 0 Ω jumper resistors

anomalies.impact: With both modes populated, the two GPIO outputs are tied together through about 2k of resistance and the servo signal pins are also driven by the RS-485 driver output. The two GPIO nets can fight each other, and the bus driver can contend with the MCU outputs, so the servos may not respond correctly in either mode.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows a few suspicious items: the MAX3485 footprint does not match its library footprint filter, and the serial-bridge jumpers R15/R22 are populated alongside the PWM path, which conflicts with the mutually exclusive mode design. The spec's reference designators do not map cleanly onto the netlist, so these findings are of moderate-to-low confidence.
